question.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthogonal?

I. $U=\{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -20\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $V=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $W=\{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
$\{{u}_{1},{u}_{2},{u}_{3}\},$ 
$\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\},$ and 
$\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2},{w}_{3}\},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthogonal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0,\,{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3}=0,\,{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3}=0.$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0.$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0,\,{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{3}=0,\,{w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{3}=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- The set $U$ cannot be orthogonal since it contains  $3$ vectors from ${R}^{2}$ (in which we can have an orthogonal set with at most 2 non-zero vectors). Therefore, $U$ is not an orthogonal set.

- For the set $V,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=0+10=10\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthogonal set.

- For the set $W,$ notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=12+3-1=14\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $W$ is not an orthogonal set.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "None of the listed".
